extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and agents (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for U.S. patent application publication, nonpublication requests, notices of foreign filing, abandonment/revival, publication fees, republication/correction, redacted publication, and public access. Guidance is specific to USPTO procedures and relevant CFR/35 U.S.C. provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of foreign filing required within 45 days
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant who has submitted a nonpublication request subsequently files an application directed to the invention in another country, or under a multilateral international agreement that requires publication of applications eighteen months after filing, the applicant must notify the Office of such filing within forty-five days after the date of the filing of such foreign or international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely notify the Office shall result in abandonment of the U.S. application (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii)). Form PTO/SB/36 (revision April 2001 or later) may be used to both rescind a nonpublication request and provide notice of foreign filing. The benefit of a certificate of mailing or transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 will be given to a notice of foreign filing. If the 45th day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Federal holiday within DC, filing on the next succeeding business day is timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions triggering the notice-of-foreign-filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must timely file a notice of foreign filing to avoid abandonment of a U.S. application if: (A) applicant filed a nonpublication request in the U.S. application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a); (B) applicant subsequently filed a foreign or international application directed to the invention disclosed in the U.S. application that requires publication 18 months after filing; and (C) applicant did not rescind the nonpublication request before filing the foreign or international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the nonpublication request was rescinded before the foreign filing then the 45-day notice requirement does not apply; merely rescinding without filing the notice of foreign filing within 45 days will result in abandonment and require revival under 37 CFR 1.137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to provide timely notice of foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii) provides that failure to provide the required notice of foreign filing within 45 days of the subsequent filing of a counterpart application shall result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When abandonment occurs by operation of this statute, the applicant’s sole remedy to restore the application is filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 to revive the abandoned application on the basis of unintentional delay. The Office may not recognize the abandonment in its systems or notify applicant, so applicants who determine the notice was not timely should promptly file a petition to revive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival petition requirements under 37 CFR 1.137
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantable petition to revive on the basis of unintentional delay must be accompanied by: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); (3) any terminal disclaimer (and fee) required pursuant to paragraph (d); and (4) a statement that the entire delay in filing the required reply was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information. Form PTO/SB/64a may be used for such a petition to revive. In cases where abandonment is pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii) for failure to notify of foreign filing, the reply requirement of paragraph (c) is met by the notification of such filing, but filing the petition will not operate to stay any period for reply that may be running against the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the reply for revival (37 CFR 1.137(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application abandoned under 37 CFR 1.57(a), the reply must include a copy of the specification and any drawings of the previously filed application. In an application abandoned for failure to pay issue/publication fee, the required reply must include payment of the fee or outstanding balance. In a nonprovisional application abandoned for failure to prosecute, the required reply may be met by the filing of a continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics depend on cause of abandonment; payment of required fees or filing of terminal disclaimer may also be required. The petition to revive will not stay other running reply periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment to avoid publication (37 CFR 1.138(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking to abandon an application to avoid publication must submit a declaration of express abandonment by way of a petition under this paragraph including the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h) in sufficient time to permit officials to recognize the abandonment and remove the application from the publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect the petition will not be granted and the application will be published in regular course unless such declaration and petition are received more than four weeks prior to the projected date of publication. Forms PTO/AIA/24A (for apps filed on/after Sept 16, 2012) or PTO/SB/24A (for earlier apps) may be used. Filing electronically via EFS-Web increases the chance the petition is timely received. If not recognized at least four weeks prior, the Office cannot avoid publication; once recognized, an express abandonment cannot be revived if publication already occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee payment timing and effect (37 CFR 1.211(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d) must be paid in each application published under this section before the patent will be granted. The sum specified in the Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due will include the publication fee which must be paid within three months from the date of mailing of the notice to avoid abandonment. This three-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is not published, the publication fee (if paid) will be refunded. The small entity discount is not available for the publication fee. If an RCE is filed after a Notice of Allowance is mailed (but before the three-month expiration), the Office will suspend the publication fee due date until three months from the mail date of the new Notice of Allowance. Effective Jan 1, 2014 the publication fee was $0.00; requests for refund may be submitted after 4 weeks from issue date if the application did not publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Publication and revised publication dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be informed of the projected publication date assigned to the application on the filing receipt. The Office will mail a “Notice of Publication” to the applicant indicating that the application has been published when the application is published. A “Notice of New or Revised Publication Date” may be mailed if the publication date changes by more than six weeks due to processing delays, removal of a secrecy order, or revival of an abandoned application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant timely adds/deletes a benefit or priority claim and the Office recognizes the correction before technical preparations begin, the Office will mail a corrected filing receipt informing applicant of the newly assigned projected publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of published applications and electronic access (37 CFR 1.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application publications are available electronically on the USPTO website. Any member of the public may obtain status information concerning any published application via PAIR. The file of an abandoned published application is available to the public as set forth in 37 CFR 1.11(a); copies of application-as-filed, file contents, or specific documents may be provided upon request and payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.19(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may at its discretion provide access to only an electronic copy of the specification, drawings, and file contents. Published applications scanned into the Image File Wrapper (IFW) may be available electronically via PAIR. If a redacted copy was used for publication, the copy provided may be limited to the redacted copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for early publication (37 CFR 1.219)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that will be published may be published earlier than the 18-month date at the request of the applicant. Any request for early publication must be accompanied by the publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant does not submit a copy of the application in compliance with Office electronic filing requirements pursuant to 37 CFR 1.215(c), the Office will publish as provided in 37 CFR 1.215(a). No consideration will be given to requests for publication on a certain date; such requests are treated as a request for publication as soon as possible. The publication process takes approximately 14 weeks and does not begin until the application is complete and ready for publication (e.g., executed oath/declaration filed and filing fee paid). If early publication is requested and publication fee paid, applicant will not be required to pay the publication fee at allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for republication requirements (37 CFR 1.221(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for republication of an application previously published must include a copy of the application in compliance with the Office electronic filing system requirements and be accompanied by the publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d) and the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request does not comply with these requirements or the copy does not comply with EFS requirements, the Office will not publish the application and will refund the publication fee. While there is no set time limit for requesting republication, the application must still be pending. If the application has been recognized as abandoned or has issued as a patent, the application may be removed from the publication process and not republished, even if the Office accepted the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for corrected publication—material mistake standard (37 CFR 1.221(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a request for a corrected or revised patent application publication only when the Office makes a material mistake which is apparent from Office records. A request for a corrected publication under 37 CFR 1.221(b) must be filed within two months from the date of the patent application publication (this period is not extendable) and must identify the Office’s material mistake in the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A material mistake is one that affects the public’s ability to appreciate the technical disclosure or determine the scope of provisional rights. Examples include omission of claims that were included in the originally-filed specification and not canceled by a preliminary amendment; omission of part of the specification that provides support for the published claims; omission of originally-filed drawings; omission of a timely submitted benefit claim in specified contexts. The request should include a listing of alleged material errors, marked-up copies of relevant pages, and an indication of where in the specification as filed the relevant text appears. If the period has expired or the mistake is caused by the applicants, applicants should request republication under 37 CFR 1.221(a) instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-material mistakes (not grounds for corrected publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not file requests for corrected publication that include no material error made by the Office. Errors in the correspondence address, assignment information or missing assignment information, minor typographical errors, missing section headings, a failure to include an amendment, or similar matters are not material mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: publication did not include assignment information; publication shows the wrong assignee or a misspelled assignee name; publication did not include a benefit or priority claim to a prior application due to applicant’s failure to timely file or properly submit the reference; publication did not include claims or changes submitted in an amendment; typographical errors that do not affect interpretation of published claims. Filing corrected-publication requests for non-material errors is discouraged; incorrect requests may result in a patent term adjustment reduction where Office made only non-material errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for requests for corrected publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a corrected publication under 37 CFR 1.221(b) must be filed within two months from the date of the patent application publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This two-month time period is not extendable. If the period has expired, correct mistakes by filing a request for republication under 37 CFR 1.221(a), not a corrected-publication request under 1.221(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted publication eligibility and timing (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(v) and 37 CFR 1.217)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant has filed applications in one or more foreign countries and such foreign-filed applications or their descriptions are less extensive than the U.S. application, the applicant may submit a redacted copy of the U.S. application eliminating any part or description not also contained in the corresponding foreign applications. The Director may only publish the redacted copy unless the redacted copy is not received within 16 months after the earliest effective filing date for which a benefit is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisions of 35 U.S.C. 154(d) shall not apply to a claim if the description published in the redacted application does not enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the subject matter of the claim. The redacted copy must be submitted in compliance with EFS requirements; the title must correspond to the application title at time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted copy submission requirements (37 CFR 1.217(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The redacted copy of the application must be submitted in compliance with the Office electronic filing system requirements. The applicant must concurrently submit in paper: (1) a certified copy of each foreign-filed application that corresponds to the application for which a redacted copy is submitted; (2) a translation of each such foreign-filed application that is in a language other than English, and a statement that the translation is accurate; (3) a marked-up copy of the application showing the redactions in brackets; and (4) a certification that the redacted copy eliminates only the part or description not contained in any corresponding foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the redacted copy does not comply with EFS requirements, the Office will publish the application as provided in 37 CFR 1.215(a). Submission must be timely within 16 months of the earliest effective filing date for which benefit is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing submission and certification requirements when filing a redacted copy (37 CFR 1.217(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a redacted copy is submitted, the Office will provide a copy of the complete file wrapper and contents to any person upon written request unless the applicant complies with additional requirements. Applicant must accompany the redaction submission with copies of any Office correspondence and prior submissions showing desired redactions and second copies showing the redacted material in brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to the initial submission, applicant must: (i) within one month of the date of mailing of any Office correspondence, file a copy of such correspondence including any desired redactions and a second copy showing the redacted material in brackets; and (ii) with each submission by applicant, include a copy including desired redactions and a second copy showing redacted material in brackets. Each such submission must be accompanied by the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i) and a certification that the redactions are limited to elimination of material relevant only to parts not contained in the redacted copy submitted for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Office paper/electronic handling on publication/corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant does not submit a copy in compliance with the Office electronic filing system requirements, the Office will publish the application as provided in 37 CFR 1.215(a) and may dismiss requests that do not meet EFS requirements. The Office cannot ensure removal from publication any time after the publication process is initiated (about 4 months prior to projected publication date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EFS-Web for timely receipt and to increase the chances filings (petitions, express abandonment, redacted copies, republication requests) are recognized in sufficient time. The publication process takes approximately 14 weeks and begins only when application is complete and ready for publication (executed oath/declaration filed and filing fee paid).
